Fitarc Pull Up Assist Bands,Pull Up Resistance Bands for Chin Up,Adjustable Pullup Bands I remember as a young man I used to be able to do 10 pull ups. 30+ years later, I tried to do a pull-up and couldn't even do one - not even half of one, actually. It's been 6 months, and I am still working on 2. Someone told me that this is because I'm not going through the whole pull-up motion often enough to build the muscles and that I should go to a gym and use a machine that gives you an assist so you can go through repetitions of the whole motion - over time, the assist is then reduced without reducing the number of repetitions. Well, I live too far from a gym - so I got these assist bands. And the first time I tried them after installation, I did 5 pull-ups - and could have done more! Starting tomorrow I will do 10 pull-ups and then reduce the number of straps over time.

The only downside to this solution is that if you don't have your pull-up bars installed high enough, you have to fiddle around with the strap length or put your knees in the stirrup instead of the feet. But that's not the bands' fault.
text_fidelity_b: Fitarc Pull Up Assist Bands,Pull Up Resistance Bands for Chin Up,Adjustable Pullup Bands

RYOMI Sling Bag Crossbody Backpack Women Men Waterproof Shoulder Chest Outdoor Headline: I'm finding this pack to be exactly what I wanted, it's just perfect for my purposes.

Background: I've been considering getting a single-strap small pack for travel: a full-sized backpack is sometimes too big, and a fanny-pack too small. When I fly I like to have a carryon and a small pack ("personal item") for the essentials like phone, kindle, tablet, travel documents, etc. And I often find it convenient to have the same sort of thing for a long day of walking around enjoying the sights: I might carry some maps, a bottle of water or two, and so on. Finally, I want to be able to wear the pack in front sometimes, such as when I'm sitting down in a bus, or when I'm in a crowd and feel concerned about inviting a skilful thief to come up behind me.

This pack is well-constructed, lightweight, and designed thoughtfully for the kinds of things I was considering. There are three compartments, with the back one being the one where I'd stash the electronics and the documents/maps. The middle one is good for pens, cards, passport, and such. The small one in front is perfect for stowing the wallet & phone when going through security. And finally, there's a smaller pocket in the back that opens on the side, good for a book or a phone or something like that. There's also a small pocket on the strap, but it's too small for a phone, so I'm not sure what I'd use it for, really. (I find that the claims of a "hidden pocket" are silly, and I personally wouldn't hang my sunglasses on the loop on the strap.)

So overall an excellent pack that meets my needs for a small travel pack. Take a look for yourself.

Timex Personal Trainer Heart Rate Monitor Watch - Gray I had purchased this as a Christmas gift, but my wife thought she might be allergic to the chest strap. So I am using it. The watch and chest strap are well made. Here are some things you should know:

1. you must use the chest strap. You get no heart/pulse rate readings on the watch without it. The chest strap is easy on, easy off.
2. once you affix the chest strap, you will forget you have it on.
3. you need to wet a portion of the chest strap before applying it for the day. I simply put a swipe of water on each part of the strap on either side of the Timex logo. You only need do this once per day, or so I have found.
4. while you can change the battery in the chest strap yourself, the manual recommends a professional change the watch battery.
5. the manual itself requires some close attention if you are to get the full benefit of the monitor. I am still figuring out all of the bells and whistles.
6. the recorded HR on this watch matches the treadmill HR monitor at the gym as well as our BP machine.

When I read that other reviewers bought this item based on their heart doctor's suggestion, I thought that was good enough for me. My wife's loss is my gain (smile)!

UPDATE, March 14,2013
I continue to enjoy the use of this product immensely. Note that when you are not using the HR monitor feature, it serves as a timepiece. And finally, a note to those who, like me, are hearing impaired. On the first day I used this monitor, I went to see my hearing aid dispenser for a check-up. He immediately said, "What's beeping?" I said, is it my phone? He said no, it seems to be coming from . . . there. He meant the monitor on my wrist! I myself could not hear it a lick! So: if you see a tiny chime icon on the watch face in monitor mode, then anyone close to you can hear what I surmise are rhythmic beeps. The chime feature can be turned off, as I discovered after I spent a half-day announcing my presence to the world!

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak Chute Mag Vacuum Insulated I love to have water with me. The problem is that the containers either are too hard to get into especially when I only have one hand available, or they spill on me, or the caps flap back onto my face making me dribble water all over. Let's see how this container performed.

WHAT IS THIS BOTTLE LIKE?
This bottle is thick. It is stainless steel with a painted black bottom on it. It has a wide opening of about 2 1/4 inches wide. It is double walled and stainless steel inside too. The top is thick plastic. It has a handle built into it, and it screws onto the bottom nicely. The cap of the bottle screws on with inside threads (not outside) and it snaps back so that a magnet holds the cap against the side of the top so it stays out of the way when drinking.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This container is amazing. I have put cold water in the bottle with no ice and after about four hours in close to 100 degrees the water was still cool. I have put ice in this container and the water has stayed cold for two days- although it was not near 100 degrees all of that time.

The handle is easy to carry, and the cap stays out of the way perfectly. This is easy to drink from and I am thriled that it also fits into my car cup holders without tipping over. That may not be the case with every car, but with mine it is.

EASY TO CLEAN
The opening is large enough to get a good bottle brush in there to clean it with. It is wider than many other containers I have used.

ANY PROBLEMS?
The only thing I am not fond of is the plastic piece that folds to hold the cap onto the container. It seems like a flimsy connection of plastic and I can see it breaking down quickly. I will update my review should that happen.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a nice sturdy container to keep liquids cold for at least a day or more, this is a wonderful purchase. It is easy to carry, great to drink from and has a large enough hole to make it easy to clean too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! This is my favorite container of this type so far.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Chute Mag Vacuum Insulated

SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer Essentially a marriage between Bosu and regular steppers, this device promises to bring the best of both to the home exercise routine. While it does a provide an acceptable basic workout, it does not quite make the mark.

The device itself is large and bulky. You must inflate it with a really lame hand pump. I thought the pump was flimsy. There are no valves, just holes that are plugged after inflation. Once inflated, it is essentially two firm air cushions topped with a balance board. I did find that it held its air, which was good since I do not relish another round with the hand pump. The enclosed dvd comes with instructions and workouts. If you have resistance bands, you are good to go.If not, you need to purchase some because they are not included. The workouts are basic and unlikely to challenge advanced and intermediate exercisers. Overall, this is not a terribly successful hybrid. There is some wobble but probably not enough to make a significant difference in the workout.

As tempting as this concept was, I did not find it superior to or a replacement for either my regular stepper or Bosu. Although the device itself is sturdy, the cost cutting short cuts (hand pump, no valves, no resistance bands) detract. If you are a beginner with a craving for novelty, this device might be a good choice. But overall, I thought it failed to realize its promise.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
OASMU Sand Free Beach Blanket Picnic Mat I live in an area about equidistant from the beach and the mountains. I like going to the beach but I much prefer the mountains, particularly in the autumn when the leaves change. One of the simple pleasures in life is having a picnic in the mountains, and this particular beach blanket is a good accessory for those trips.

This is not a blanket in the traditional sense. There is no padding, no fiber, no fringe. This is a very thin cover made of parachute nylon and it is very lightweight and thin. It will not provide any insulation from hard ground, nor will it provide much in the way of drying off after getting wet, but it is very water resistant and it will keep you from getting wet from wet ground unless you put it down on standing water.

Because this is such a lightweight blanket it means that it can be caught up with a good gust of wind. Provision has been made for that. There are pockets on the corners and they can be filled with sand at the beach or with stones when farther away. There are also loops on the corners for securing with pegs. Unfortunately there are no pegs included with this blanket and that is the one thing I would suggest for improvement.

I have a special use for this blanket. Along the Blue Ridge parkway there are picnic areas and my family and I like to go there for a nice picnic lunch. The blanket makes a perfect (although very large) tablecloth for the picnic table. When we’re done, it is very easy to clean and it packs up for the next trip with little effort.

I love the fact that this blanket compacts down to a size smaller than a football. It folds up very neatly and compactly and it fits in a pretty blue nylon bag with a pull tie. At that size it is small enough to fit in a shoulder bag or in just about any space in the car when traveling.

This is a very well-made blanket, too. I have found no issues with the stitching, the seams are straight and there are no nicks or cuts in the nylon material. I imagine that will change over years of use, but so far it still is pristine.

I am very happy with this beach blanket. It serves me well on picnics in the mountains, which is really all I could ask for. It is made well, it’s plenty large, and there are some thoughtful features that went into it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: OASMU Sand Free Beach Blanket Picnic Mat

KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO I have 7 scooters I've collected along the way to review and hands down this is the most fun one out there! If you're familiar with how an electric scooter works then this one is just like the others and will be easy to setup and get going. Took me about five minutes to unbox and get going! Even for newbies this scooter is plenty easy to setup!

One of the favorite things I love on this are the giant wheels- we ride on a concrete trail several miles across town and this absolutely grabs onto the concrete very well and is a better overall ride! My one complaint is the tires must be thin as on my fourth ride, one of them got a flat even though I didn't hit anything noticeable like glass or a screw. Nothing in the tire but it just started losing pressure on a ride and within a couple minutes the tire was completely flat and I was stuck pushing it home a mile. My suggestion is to get the tire size off the tire and immediately swap them out for solid tires! The air tires are a slightly smoother ride but you'll regret it when you're stuck pushing it home...
Edit: The air leaks out of the valve stem. I went to add some green slime and it did hold air but when I moved the valve stem, air comes out at the bottom of it... So the valve stem was faulty and the slime didn't help anything. I've been searching like crazy with no luck finding a solid tire to replace these with. Should have been on the scooter to begin with in my opinion.

Speed wise, I got this monster up to 29 mph and I'm a larger man (260 pounds) so that's a testament to this thing! It stands higher than your average scooter too which is weird at first but I fell in love with the added height nearly instantly!

It has a faster startup than other scooters that require more of a kick start. Which- be careful, that can be dangerous if you have the scooter on and are pushing it to park it before turning it off. I almost flipped mine backwards onto myself this way, it happens QUICK. So definitely turn the scooter (and any scooter) off before pushing around.

Battery life is fantastic- we ride several miles across town and back and I still have half a battery left after that!

Overall this is my favorite thing I've gotten on review and I've gotten big fancy electronics like big TVs, computers, etc... But this is my favorite toy I've grabbed, I HIGHLY recommend it! In the future I'll absolutely be buying another from this company!
text_fidelity_b: KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO

BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids. I purchased this to use on my bicycle that I use for commuting. I leave early in the morning while it is still dark. The route I take is pretty well lit with street lights so I use the lights mostly for visibility and not to light the road in front of me.

The mounts are pretty simple to use. I attached the front to the handlebar and the back to the basket I have on the rear rack. The front light has 3 steady settings at 3 levels of brightness and one flashing mode. I am not sure how useful the level of brightness would be in absolute darkness as far as seeing the path in front of you because I have not used it in that scenario, but it seems pretty bright to me. I keep it on flashing mode for visibility. It is conveniently re-chargeable via USB cord and it seems to last adequately between charges.

I gave this product a 3 star rating because the back light does not work the way I need it to. The first time I used it, I thought I turned it on but when I got to my destination it was off so I figured I forgot to turn it on. The second time I used it on the return trip, I made absolutely sure it was on when I started and when I got to the destination it was off again. I took the light off my bike and turned it on and dropped it onto a hard surface from a distance of less than 3 inches and it shut off. Since this is battery operated and not rechargeable, I'm guessing the batteries get jolted from going over a bump on the road and shuts off on its own. It lights up again without any issues if you press the on button again, but that is not feasible or safe to reach behind you and fix it if you are riding on a road with vehicular traffic all around you. It is also very inconvenient to pull over to the side every time it shuts off to turn it back on again. Since the light set was fairly inexpensive, I just purchased a different separate backlight from the local box store to replace it.

I will not go through the time and inconvenience of returning the item or exchanging it because it simply is not worth it. I hope the seller doesn't try to contact me to "fix" the problem because they will be wasting their time.
text_fidelity_b: BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids.

I first tried it just as a spray-and-wait cleaner and found, while it did lighten things up a bit (I’m using it on plastic chairs and webbing), it was not all that effective. But, when sprayed on, let sit a bit, and then scrubbed with a soft bristle scrub brush, things worked much better.

It’s not too bad in terms of smell. Granted, you won’t be tempted to dab a bit behind each ear but compared with bleach, this is not bad at all. It does require a good bit of rinsing with clean water to get rid of all traces of the cleaner, especially after use with a scrubber.

It’s not an amazing cleaner, but it gets the job done. A solid 4-stars.

text_fidelity_a: V12 Fitness & Health Smartwatch with Activity Tracker 24/7 Heart Rate Monitor Blood Oxygen Spo2 Scientific Sleep Monitor IP68 Waterproof Exercise Sports Pedometer Watch for Running Walking (Grey) I got this watch because it needs to be charged every day or every other day. I also got this because it states it is waterproof. That is not true. The IP in IP68 stands for Ingress Protection. The 6 stands for prevents dust entering the insides. The 8 means suitable for immersing underwater for an indefinite period at any depth. But the manufacture determines the depth and length of time. So, it is not truly waterproof. In fact, the included instructions indicate you should not soak the device, do not wear to swim, dive or take hot showers. You can wash your hands and take a cold shower. The general rule for IP68, is that it prevents dust from getting in and you can be in the water for up to 30 minutes for 1.5 meters. And never submerge in salt water.
text_fidelity_b: V12 Fitness & Health Smartwatch with Activity Tracker 24/7 Heart Rate Monitor Blood Oxygen Spo2 Scientific Sleep Monitor IP68 Waterproof Exercise Sports Pedometer Watch for Running Walking (Grey)

If the bag is turned upside down for any reason the pistols can easily come out of the pocket they're stowed in and if you're carrying two as the bag is designed for, they can then bang into one another potentially causing damage to one or both. The divider will keep them from striking the magazines but not from hitting each other. The magazine pouches are, at least now while new, quite tight and hold my 10 and 12 round Sig Sauer P365 magazines tightly in place. Even vigorous shaking didn't dislodge them. The outside pocket had a good size gusset and expands to hold a box of 100 9mm rounds and my Uplula loader with room to spare. It also has a large velcro area for membership patches, flags, etc. The carry handles are comfortable. I wish there was a more secure way to hold your pistols in place and I plan on trying to modify the bag myself to achieve this. Speedo Aqua Fit Swim Training Gloves First of all, many thanks to all the other reviewers who mentioned that these run large. I wear a XL glove, so I was going to order this in XL. Very glad I didn't - the L size fits just fine, and now that I have one, it's clear the XL would have been too big. That tip from the other reviewers saved me some return postage - thanks!

In terms of the actual glove, it's great. Fits fine, and appears well made. Very secure velcro closure on the wrist.

I use mine for aqua aerobics and to add a "boost" to my swimming workouts. I've used the plastic hand paddle in the past - they are helpful in giving more resistance, but are rather awkward to use. These - if you'll forgive the inevitable pun - fit like a glove and don't get in the way. You can increase or decrease resistance by just expanding or closing your hand.

A word of caution - if you've never used hand paddles or webbed gloves before for exercise, go slow at first. You're putting a lot more strain on your muscles, especially the shoulders. Take it easy at first until you get a feel for the workout, then slowly increase duration and speed. A bit of care will prevent a lot of pain!

KastKing Sharky Spinning Fishing Reel Ultra Light Weight Freshwater Professional Open Face Reel With Features Found Only On Top Quality Penn Shimano Daiwa and Okuma Spinning Fishing Reels I love to go freshwater fishing and this weekend I approached the lake with a brand new weapon - a KastKing Sharky 6000 spinning reel. This is a serious reel that made a good day of fishing even better.

I will start by saying that even though it is approximately the same weight as my primary reel - a KastKing Orcas 4000 - it is significantly larger. I spooled on over 200 yards of 10-lb. test fluorocarbon line and it still had room for more line on it. I put it on an 8' limber rod and headed out to a productive spot.

I am very fussy about my reels and I expect them to meet several criteria. I want a good cast range, a smooth cast, smooth retrieve, quiet operation and a zero-reverse clutch. There has to be enough clearance between my knuckles and the bail to keep it from rapping me on the knuckles when I retrieve. And finally, the drag has to work and be easy to set. The Sharky met every one of these requirements.

I learned fast (and the hard way) that the reel is more than accommodating when it comes to casting and more than once I sent my lures into the trees instead of to the edge of the bank when I was unable to hit the bank with other reels on identical rods. This required a little adjustment on my part but it meant I did not have to work as hard and it also meant I could hit farther targets when I wanted to. So, when I fish from the bank I have a better range into whatever water I am fishing.

The retrieve is glassy smooth and very fast too. Not once did I have a problem with snarled line on the retrieve when I had near-zero load which is a problem on some reels. I like that I could bring in the line very quickly when needed (like for grabbing the net to assist another fisherman). The reel is quiet when spinning - not silent, but quiet.

When the ant-reverse clutch is engaged there is no reverse at all. To me this is a sign that the reel is quality made and is assembled well. I really, really dislike reels that do not have a zero-reverse clutch, and even worse is a reel that has one but it still has just a little play in it. The Sharky’s zero-reverse is solid and works exactly like it’s supposed to work - absolutely zero reverse.

The bail spins an inch or so away from my knuckles but never once has it hit my hand when spinning.

The drag set is uniform and smooth and does not really get harder to turn until close to the end of the tightening range.

In appearance this is a very attractive reel, black and red with a little bit of chrome. It is surprisingly lightweight for the size. I have bigger hands than average so a reel this size that doesn’t add much more weight is very welcome.

The reel helped me land a good variety of fish including largemouth bass, crappie and a near-citation yellow perch. The most exciting catch was a largemouth bass which was not huge but not small either and provided the best test of the reel under stress, and the reel brought this fish to the boat easily without incident. Even under the load of a fighting bass the reel was just as smooth in operation as when retrieving a test plug.

I am very, very pleased with the Sharky 6000 and will be using it again in the same lake in a few weeks. It has not let me down even once and it works very well. If you want a larger reel that works great and does not add a lot of weight to your gear, take a very close look at this reel.

text_fidelity_a:
Rayovac SE3DLNBL Sportsman 240 Lumen 3D LED Lantern, Blue After Hurricane Sandy hit the east coast and I was without power for 9 days, I decided to purchase one more light to add to my army of 13 flashlights. I wanted something that would illuminate a room better than my underwater flashlight and my headlamp. My underwater flashlight and head lamp happen to be exceptional lights but they can only be used for focused tasks since they lack a wide range. This lantern not only gives exceptional light but it also illuminates an entire small room.

These are the many features I like:

- The lantern is so bright it is blinding but it definitely lights up my kitchen from 1/2 a room away. I just had to make sure I did not look the light in the eye.
- It has a high and low mode.
- It can also be used as a strobe light (meaning in blinking mode).
- It only takes only 3 D size batteries (only one more battery than most D-battery flashlights).
- It's water resistant.
- It comes with a lifetime warranty.
- The lantern has a tent hook on the bottom; although it is a bit difficult to move.
- It also has an EZ-find light that blinks every few seconds; although that "find" light (which sits above the black power button) is barely visible in the dark.
- Customer service is excellent.

The only problem I had with this light is that it did not come with any instructions; it only comes with a wrap-around paper touting its virtues. Therefore, I had to call the company on the 800 I found on the Internet (you can find that # in my comments) to learn how to make the strobe light work. I also asked how the EZ find light worked because I was unable to detect it.

The tent hook and handle are self-explanatory but to make this light work, this is what I had to do. Please note I executed all these instructions with the front of the lantern facing me:

1. Both the top and bottom of the lantern screw off. The top is where the blub is and that can be screwed off counter-clockwise but there's really no reason to remove the top. I screwed off the bottom clockwise and inserted the 3 D batteries as indicated on the stickers inside. I then lined up the red arrows (both on lid and case) when closing the bottom in the opposite direction I opened it and made I heard it click shut.

2. I pushed the black button to operate the light. Pressing it once brought on high mode and pressing it again brought on low mode. Sometimes I found that after one press no light comes on; in that case I pressed it again until I was in the desired mode. The tech said this was normal behavior.

3. To get the strobe light working, I had to HOLD down the black button for about 5 or 6 seconds until the light started to flash. I then pressed the black button to turn the strobe effect off.

4. To see the EZ find light that is located above the black on off button, I moved the lantern to a totally dark room. This light flashed every 5 or 6 seconds but I still found it hard to see.

In summary, this is a great lantern for illuminating a small room or anywhere I need to illuminate a larger area than a flashlight can provide. The light given off seems fluorescent but it's bright enough to work with. The only thing I did not like is that instructions on how to operate the strobe, insert the batteries, etc. were not provided. Although I was able to figure out how to do most of this, I had no clue I had to HOLD down the on/off button for 5 or 6 seconds to get the strobe feature to work. Since this lantern is going into storage until I need it, I will take out the batteries as the EZ find light will probably drain them after a couple of months.
text_fidelity_b: Rayovac SE3DLNBL Sportsman 240 Lumen 3D LED Lantern, Blue

Survival Kits, for Camping, Hiking, Outdoor Adventure Emergency kit, 14 in 1 Survival kit for Men, is The for Your Adventurous Friends, Lovers Lots of stuff in a small-ish package. I was actually pretty impressed with the quality of some of the items with all you get for the price-point. So lets dive right in.

Pros:
- Knife. Sharp and functional. Comes with a seatbelt cutter, blade locks well and come with a functional EDC belt clip. Handles well in hand. Also comes with a glass breaking tip on opposit end.
- Tactical Pen is solid. Writes well and the pointy tip does look like it could easily break glass. Also comes with a functional belt or pocket clip.
- Flashlight is also functional and bright. Cannot tell how many lumens, but bright enough for camp use. You do have to provide your own battery but I am ok with that.
- The Spork with knife is also functional. Although you have to be careful with the knife end as its very sharp. You get a whisle that you can cover the knife end. Not sure it makes sense to have a knife and spork in the same tang seeing you also get an external knife, but it works along with the can opener.
- Drinking straw is ok but I would recommend a designated filtered drinking straw for a emergency pack-out.
- The wood-cutting wire-saw, is just like any other. it ok, but again, having an axe or foldable saw is also what I would highly recommend in an survival packout.
- The brass compass actually surprised me. Its functional and compared to higher quality brands it works.
- Fire-stick also works but could use a longer lanyard.
- Pocket/wallet tool is functional and sharp, be careful. I does come in its own sheath but you will want one better, more durable.
- One suprising feature is that I received both a philip and flat-head mini-screw driver. Not mini in the sense of precision screwdrivers but more for light work. Functaional and nice to keep around.
- Braclet with whistle is functional however more on the compass later. The included fire-starter does throw off sparkens when used.

Cons:
- Missing the extra water bottle holder. I received the black one but not the coyote tan one.
- Caribener is only for light duty work. The screw locking feature can easily undue itself after use. Don't recommend. you can get better.
- The compass on the braclet is garbage. Use the other one that comes with the kit. I tried to move away the fire-starter and any other metals close by but still wouldn't find north. Haven't tried it outside away from other metal objects, but again, use the compass that came with the kit.
- The box is made of a cheap plastic, not polymer. It's not sealable so if you are ok with that, then it 'works' but if you want to a higher quality box, that is sealable, look for one seperately or a kit that comes with a quality one.
- The nylon lanyards is nothing to write home about. Get parachord instead.

Final Conclusion: For the price and what you get, this is ok for an entry level gift to someone or even for yourself. For those that take survialist and serious campers/backpackers/hikers, there are better quality items. I usually just buy individual quality items and box them together. But this isn't bad. I would rate it 4.5 if it came with all the items it advertized.

I'm 5'9" and around 200# and can throw a decent set of punches and round houses. I expected it to lean some, but only a few punches, even mid-power, causes the whole thing to dance around. I had it on carpet, then put it on a foam pad on the carpet. Nothing kept it from moving around. My son (9 yo) can get a bunch more punches it without it moving too much, but it still moves. I see other reviews say to use sand, so I might go that route.
It appears the seal for the cap does not keep the base water tight. After a short while, water is escaping and dribbling down the sides. It's not a huge deal, but unexpected.
The top portion does have a natural lean to it - it's not straight up. I don't have an opinion on that yet.
All the bad out of the way, it is relatively easy to adjust the height, even my son was able to bring it from a setting well over his head down. It's also a lot of fun to hit and is a good workout.

text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack 50 Lb iSelect Adjustable Dumbbells, Works with Alexa, Sold as Pair These dumbbells are very sturdy and look like serious business!
I got these during prime day, price seem competitive at $300 and the adjustment system was a plus.
One of the problems I have with these is space, since they need to be in their cradle, they take up more space than two separate dumbbells each in their own base. So for a spaced constrained home gym like mine, this is a disadvantage.
Main issue I had and reason why I'm returning is because I couldn't really used them due to a firmware upgrade issue. I received them during the weekend, assembled (minimum required), and tested them and they worked fine, when adjusting the knob, the necessary plates would be selected.
However, a couple of days later as I was ready for my first workout I downloaded the app and proceeded with registration and so on. As part of the process the firmware got updated. After that, the knob doesn't work and I can't adjust weight. If I cycle power I can adjust once or twice and then it becomes non responsive again. So I created a ticket for support, but got a response for a different product. Then I called in, we tried to do a hardware reset and it didn't work. So the agent said that she already had four similar calls, that I should either return or wait for a new base that can take several weeks.
Waiting for that long is not an option for me, so I have to return. I wish the company would give me another option, like replacing with a set of regular adjustable dumbbells instead of these smart ones.
It is concerning, considering this is a company that basically sells smart connected products, that they can have such low quality software upgrades that brick your device and then you have to wait weeks for it to be fixed. I'd think twice before getting more expensive equipment from Nordictrack.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack 50 Lb iSelect Adjustable Dumbbells, Works with Alexa, Sold as Pair

text_fidelity_a:
Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins with Mesh Bag, Yellow, Large/X-Large I really wanted to like these black and yellow Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins size LG--XLG with the adjustable heal strap and open heel. I needed a size 11 short fin for long distance endurance swimming in a harness in my pool year-round. I did not need a fin that was too buoyant and would make me lazy in my kicking.

I compared the yellow and black Phantom Aquatics Speed Sport Adjustable Snorkeling Fins L/XL (size 9-13); the US Swim Divers Grey and Black Large Fitness Fins; the black and yellow Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins size LG--XLG; the SEAC Black (Large 9.5 --11) Fins with the fixed heal strap and open heel; and the TYR BP Burner Fins LG (size 11 -- Blue & Black).

First off I had to send back the large SEAC's and large TYR EP Burner's to get the XL size in each. Both of them were painfully tight on my size 11 feet.

The worst first. The yellow and black Phantom Aquatics Speed Sport Adjustable Snorkeling Fins L/XL (size 9-13) are for snorkeling and not for training of any kind. The boot and heel strap are amazingly comfortable and strong, but the composite fin is too long and whippy for training in either a pool or open water. I would not even want to do kick sets with these. I personally would not even want to use these for snorkeling because I would always be waiting for the tips of my fins to catch up to what I was trying to do in the water to position myself for snorkeling/sightseeing.

The disappointment next. The U.S. Swim Divers Large Fitness Fins had an open heel which I generally prefer because I wear different booties during the 12 months of the year. The length of the boot was perfect, the heel strap was strong, easily adjusted, and comfortable, and the boots felt really comfortable in shape and foot support EXCEPT for the constant pressure on the knuckle of the little toe on each foot. I'm absolutely a typical size 11, but they hurt my foot, and if you have a slightly thicker or wider size 10.5--11 foot go up to the XL. I personally didn't order the next size up because while I was kicking with them I could really feel that this fin was not stiff enough for training, and certainly not for kick sets. The rubber fin was bending too easily on every kick at the seam just beyond my toes on both fins - IMOP a serious design flaw for a "fitness fin." I could never do kick sets in these, but I could use these for snorkeling since the tips of the fins do spring back almost quickly enough to be responsive to my changes in direction and speed.

SO COMFORTABLE BUT SO LONG. The black and yellow Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins size LG--XLG had a great shaped boot, a strong, easily adjusted, and flexible heel strap, and they were absolutely the MOST comfortable boot of all those I tried, BUT these were definitely a better snorkeling fin and/or an open-water training fin. They were absolutely strong enough for open water training (which I rarely get to do anymore), but too way too long for endurance training in a pool with a harness. If these were 2 inches shorter they would have been my overall pick of a stiff training fin.

I liked the way the SEAC Black Fins looked, but had to go up to the X-Large (11-12.5) and they were perfect. They have the fixed heal strap which I usually don't prefer, but this one is strong and stretchy enough to be very comfortable. The open heel did not make my feet feel unsupported at all. With barefeet they were a little soft, but with a 2mm or 5mm neoprene bootie they fit my feet perfectly. The front of the boot is comfortable lengthwise and widthwise, and there's no unnecessary gimmics in the fin design. As the ad says these are ideal for open water snorkeling for a good swimmer, and ideal for pool training. The fin is short enough and stiff enough for what I wanted to do. I can do flutter kicks or slow subtle kicks just to keep my feet afloat when I am working on my upper body. The fins do not add any extra buoyancy which I don't need with easy kicking or with a wetsuit on six months of the year. I am so glad I loved these.

I just had to try something new with the TYR BP Burner Fins LG (size 11 -- Red & Black). They had to be exchanged for the XL - the Blue and Black, and I feared they might be too big, but I found they have a very stretchy and supportive heel pocket, that was as comfortable and supportive as the adjustable heel straps I usually prefer. The TYR EP Burners boot will be my spring and summer fins as they fit my naked foot or with a 2mm bootie perfectly. It's good that the fin is just that short because just another inch or so and the fin would be too flexible. Perfect design by TYR for a training fin. As the ad says "The perfect fins for training at race cadence." I kept these for warmer water training and the SEAC's for cold water training. I would use each of these for snorkeling, as I am a strong swimmer and I want my fins to be very responsive to the demand I am putting on them to change direction or to accelerate and change speed.

I was not asked to give this review or compensated by anyone. Happy training.
text_fidelity_b: Cressi Palau Short Snorkeling Fins with Mesh Bag, Yellow, Large/X-Large

JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control (Method 38)

It’s been years since I played Ping Pong and back then I never had the opportunity to use, and was not even familiar with the Joola brand unfortunately. As I have had time to use and play with these 5 different Joola Ping Pong paddles, I must say that they are all incredible compared to any other Ping Pong paddle I have ever used. The quality and performance far exceeds my previous experiences.

Each of these paddles have been designed for a specific purpose which include speed, spin and control. Now not being a professional, I can not “honestly” say that I notice the difference between any of these five different paddles, in any of the different design aspects while using them. However, I can honestly say that visually I can tell the difference by the different rubber padding (sandwiched between the inner and outer rubber) used in each. Some have a slightly different thickness, weight, color and I assume different “springiness”. With that said, each and every one of them have performed absolutely stellar in every way for my, and my family’s play style. Personally they all have incredible spin, speed and control capabilities. They are all built with beautiful build quality, and designed with comfort and balance in mind. I especially love the resin looking inlaid logo at the end of the handles. I realise that it doesn’t make a performance difference but it just ads to the overall beauty and gives each paddle a quality looking finish.

Overall I feel quite privileged to have had the opportunity to use and experience the Joola brand and share my opinions, though I feel absolutely unqualified to have done so. Just know that if you have never used or played with a “quality” Ping Pong paddle, you are truly missing out, and this Joola brand will be the only brand I choose from here on out! The quality is impeccable!!

This intrigued me because the hoop is tighter to the body, and having the weighted ball gives me an idea of what I need my body to do. It makes more sense than a plain hoola hoop.

text_fidelity_a:
SCHWINN Fitness 430 Elliptical Machine Wow! This elliptical has all the bells and whistles!
I'll go item by item, since there are so many noteworthy features:

**Ease of Assembly: 5 stars
The manual covered everything, and while it took some time to put together this massive box of parts, everything went smoothly and came out perfectly. For you ladies and smaller people, I was able to put it together completely alone (and am female). You probably won't need help--just some podcasts or music to entertain yourself while assembling this amazing machine, and maybe a camera phone to prove you put it together. Takes a few hours, but the feeling of accomplishment is pretty amazing.

**Features and Settings: 4 stars
You can enter user data with age, height, and gender, to get better and more accurate results. Combined with sensors that let you see your heart rate, you can see what sort of activity you are doing (cardiovascular, fat burning, etc.), BUT the heart rate sensor didn't work so well for me. It kept alternating between 120bpm to 60bpm, which made me mistrust the results altogether since this was with a consistent speed, taken short times apart midway through the exercise. Other features worked great though, like different per-programmed settings such as "walk in the park", which was no such thing! It had hills and such, alternating difficulties in a smooth pattern, while some other workouts were even more challenging. The incline can also be easily adjusted to increase or decrease the overall difficulty.

**Extras: 5 stars
There is a USB port to charge your mobile or tablet device!! You can also plug into the auxiliary port to use the speakers and play music--it even comes with the cable needed! The speakers are pretty loud and clear for something like this, so it's a great add-on! There is also a three-setting fan that works well when you get hot.

**Overall workout: 5 stars
The smooth movement that is easy on your knees combined with so many extra features make this an excellent workout tool, with the quality you would expect from a quality gym. I LOVE this machine!
text_fidelity_b: SCHWINN Fitness 430 Elliptical Machine

Britax Child Bike Seat (Prior Model) Britax has been making things for children for a very long time and it enjoys a strong reputation as a company that produces quality products. The high regard myself and others have for Britax was enough to convince me to obtain this bicycle seat and I have not regretted my decision.

I have two small girls, one of whom is still small enough to use a seat such as this. The weight limit is 40 pounds, so it is only going to work for children roughly four years of age or younger. My little one is still light enough and when she was first introduced, she took to this seat right away. She likes the adventurous feeling of riding on the back of the bicycle and I feel good knowing that she is safe and secure.

Looking at the specifics of this Britax bicycle seat, the seat is very sturdy in construction and it takes about 20 minutes from the box to the point where it is ready to use. It fits most all bicycles with 26 to 28 inch wheels, which would be just about every adult bicycle manufactured. It has a built in suspension for your child's comfort and this can be a great asset if the roads or sidewalks in your area are full of potholes and bumps. The headrest has nine position settings, the footrest has fifteen positions, and the harness locks securely in place, for maximum safety. The padding can be removed and is machine washable, for added convenience, and the product carries a limited two- year warranty.

Going for a spin with a child in a small seat behind you is quite an adventure and it does take getting used to. The added weight means you have to be more careful when you stop, when you start, and how you maneuver because you always have to be mindful of the child behind you and their safety. I admit that I was a little anxious when I used this at first, but my anxiety quickly faded when I started to ride. Once you get the hang of it, like anything, it gets easier. And it is very fun for the small child in the back who gets to enjoy the sites and the excitement of riding out in the open.

All things considered, I am hard pressed to find anything wrong with this bicycle seat and I recommend it for those with small children who like the adventure and fitness they receive from riding a bicycle. I would like to ride more, and perhaps this bicycle seat will encourage me to get more active. The seat is solid in construction, fairly easy to install, and made with safety in mind. It has all the earmarks of another quality Britax product and it earns a easy recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Britax Child Bike Seat (Prior Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Sidearm Roofrack I love the ease of use of this carrier, but after buying 2 of them I learned that all you need to do is undo the quick release of the front wheel and you can wiggle the bike right out. Or you can just undo the bolts holding the arm to the bike tray and it leaves the bike fully exposed for the taking. Advertisements say you lock the carrier to the rack and your bike to the carrier, but that's not truee because of how EASY it is to get a bike out of this. At least with the velo vices and other fork mounts someone would need a hammer and they'd look suspicious whacking away to break the mount to steal your bike.

I contacted Thule and their response was "Nothing is safe... look at a car thief who can get around alarms to steal a car." I agree there are ways around things, but the way around with this carrier is just way too easy. Using the carrier as instructed should at least provide SOME security, but it does nothing. Go lock your bike on your roof and then try getting your bike out by undoing the quick release to see what I mean.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Sidearm Roofrack

Pro Art Compass Set 5pc This compass set is exactly the quality and design I was looking for at this price point. I am using this set for working in a nature journal.
What I liked:
Compass/divider sets easily and holds firmly. No screw mechanism -- simply pull/push to adjust.
The whole mechanism can be tightened or loosened with a flat head screwdriver (on my multi-tool while in the field).
Narrow slim case fits well in my field bag.
Tools lock into position in the case to keep them from shifting during hikes. Case shuts tight as well.
Very sharp points on divider - perfect for measurement work.
Ruling pen and optional holder: I like line work in my field journal, and this makes gorgeous lines with watercolor or ink. Purchased separately, a ruling pen is about $8 USD.
Easily swappable pencil/pen/divider point attachment. I use a compass to frame work in my field journal that is done at magnification.
Additional lead in tube -- nice touch!

What I didn't like...
Absolutely no instructions whatsoever, BUT the tools are intuitive for anyone who has ever used engineering/math compass sets.
A drop point attachment would have been more useful in this kit than an extension bar. (Drop points allow a compass to draw tiny circles smaller than the radius with the compass fully closed.)

Coleman 316 Series Insulated Portable Cooler with Heavy Duty Latches, Leak-Proof Outdoor High Capacity Hard Cooler, Keeps Ice for up to 5 Days I wanted to get a pretty substantial cooler to use for backyard BBQ's and for transporting a significant amount of food for long trips. I got the 120 qt cooler, which in retrospect was probably a little overkill.

There is a certain simplicity of design with this cooler. The inside is a very efficient use of space - there are no extrusions impeding the space. The cooler itself is quite sturdy and can take a grown man sitting on it. There are also 4 cup holders, but I don't see using these at all. There are two handles to maneuver the cooler, but there are no wheels, which would make it really difficult to move a cooler of this size.

So, I can't imagine bringing this cooler to a beach or to an outdoor event unless it is empty. Good luck trying to transport the cooler full of ice and drinks without wheels. This does fit perfectly in the back of a SUV or truck so it would be handy for a long drive if you need to transport a lot of food. It would also be handy for a backyard party where you don't need to move it.

Bottom line, it works well, but for the size, it should have an easier way to transport.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman 316 Series Insulated Portable Cooler with Heavy Duty Latches, Leak-Proof Outdoor High Capacity Hard Cooler, Keeps Ice for up to 5 Days

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Distance FL Trekking Pole I love these poles with the exception of a few minor things.

I love how quickly i can 'fold' these up without losing my length setting. And I love how short they fold up, and I can put them under the compression straps of my day pack. They will even fit inside if need be. Swing weight is very lite and I have had zero issue with slipping. I love the little rubber tips, which are replacable if/when they wear out. I also like the minimal baskets to allow the sections to clip together.

The few things I wish were better
The straps are fiddly to adjust and are not particularly comfortable, but not enough to be a true negative. I wish the straps had the traditional 1/2 twist rather than the method they use to have the strap lay flat under your hand. While it works, I futz with it a lot. I hope the strap issue are minimized as I use them more and strap conform to my hands better.
The handle is a little bit small and I don't have particularly large hands. Could be an issue for people with larger hands. While not really an issue for me, I plan to wrap some tennis grip around the handle.
I wish the handle had a 'trigger'.

They click a bit when using them. But I guess that is the price to pay for the quick/short break down capability. It's not a big issue but they are not as silent as say the REI carbon fiber poles, which I didn't like for various reasons but they were dead silent and had super comfy straps from day one. But that straps were even worse to adjust.

I'm really happy with these, especially for the price. As you can see the negatives were not enough for me to knock them down a star.

Sunny Sports got them out when they said they would, next day since I ordered too late for same day, And UPS as usual put them on a Donkey train, and they got there on the very last day of the expected delivery date. Since I ordered a weekend and the 5 days deliver time put them over another weekend It took 10 days. But that is not Sunny Sports fault.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Distance FL Trekking Pole

text_fidelity_a:
Rechargeable Camping Lantern, Collapsible 2200mah Battery Powered LED Lights for Tents, 3 in 1 IP66 Waterproof Emergency Flashlight for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Outages, Outdoor, Garden I have been trying to get various bug zappers to bring with my family when we go to areas that are not close to a plug. This one is interesting. Let's take a look.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a small box with instructions.

CLOSED
Closed this is used for a light. It has brighter white light, dimmed light and a warning red light.

OPEN
Open this has the ability to zap bugs.

HOW WELL DOES THIS PERFORM?
This performs well as a light, but as a bug zapper, it really is not the season for heavy bugs like we will be having later in the season. I have not been able to catch the few tiny moths in the house, nor the few tiny fruit flies. That is no surprise, however, because this zapper is not very big and these guys have been all over the house.

The light part is nice for using when necessary to see at night. During power outages it also will be handy.

HOW THIS RUNS
This runs not only on USB charging,, but also works with AAA batteries(3) which don't come with it.

CHARGE TIME
This took a couple of hours to charge up fully and it lasts a few hours depending on how it is used. I usually charge after that, so I have not let it run completely down yet.

CAN IT HANG FROM CENTER OF TENT?
This does make a good light for hanging from the center of the tent when you want to see with an overhead light. It also would do well in that position as a bug zapper. It has a handle so you can twist tie it to the loops.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For using at a camp site or on a deck in summer, this is a nice little light to have at the table at night, or use for walking at night around a camp site. As for bug zapper, in the tent, I would have to have some eye masks to sleep with. The light would be too bright for me to sleep with.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. If this turns out to be a bug zapping wonder, I will stop by and update my rating on this zapper/light. As it is now, it works, seems to do what it is supposed to do, but situations are not dire enough to see how good it really is.
text_fidelity_b: Rechargeable Camping Lantern, Collapsible 2200mah Battery Powered LED Lights for Tents, 3 in 1 IP66 Waterproof Emergency Flashlight for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Outages, Outdoor, Garden

text_fidelity_a:
2PCS Yellow LED Flash Tyre Wheel Valve Cap Light for Car Bike bicycle Motorbicycle Wheel Light Tire Light for Night Safety by TheBigThumb I initially bought this product because of the pictures and how it resembled a constant glow like in the movie TRON. I already was warned in the reviews that the product so not continuously stay on which was fine, with the cheap price it was a risk worth taking. Now that being said, when I received the product, I it not immediately obvious which light is what color. I had to set it up which was simple and test it out. These lights are motion activated with very low sensitivity, so the bumbs will need to be frequent or near constant in order for them to light up. Becuase these lights are on a wheel and the force exerted on the lights moves in a circular motion, the lights will not light up just because the wheel is spinning but rather when the tire hit a strong enough resistance in the road or rocks or gaps in the sidewalk. These lights probably wouldn't light up on a wheel that is operating on a smooth enough track or road. I tested it on my bike and the "blinking" lights were cool from a first person point of view, I have yet to test the "coolness" factor of the lights from a third person perspective (or in other words I am not geting any positive feedback from passer's by. I did not test this product on my car or on a motor cycle (like in the packaging).

With all that said, the price was low enough, the product was plastic, was shinny enough, and the performance is adequate. Overall the product is worth the risk! for cyclist or bike enthusiasts. I would definitely recommend this for the children in your family who won't care much about the quality of this inexpensive product.
text_fidelity_b: 2PCS Yellow LED Flash Tyre Wheel Valve Cap Light for Car Bike bicycle Motorbicycle Wheel Light Tire Light for Night Safety by TheBigThumb

text_fidelity_a:
Concept2 Model D Indoor Rowing Machine (Gray) This review is coming from a dumpy middle-aged woman with a hip replacement who *thought* she was going to buy a treadmill. I started comparison shopping for treadmills even though spending $1000 or more on a machine instead of just going outside for a walk seemed kind of ridiculous, even in the snow. Then I ran across an article that mentioned rowing machines as the best overall piece of home exercise equipment. Some of my college dorm mates rowed on the women's 8 and it was like the light went on. The unanimous glowing reviews for the Concept2 Model D sold me on this machine and I ordered it direct from Concept2.

After about a month I can recommend rowing without reservation. The machine itself is built like a tank. It took about 20 minutes to put it together and about 2 minutes to figure out how to separate the parts for storage. It takes about 20 seconds to actually pull the machine apart and tuck it away in a corner when I'm not using it, which I do every day. Separated, it takes up the floor space of a medium-sized refrigerator. Together, it's about 9 feet long and a possible trip hazard. I use it on a carpeted floor and haven't noticed any problems with slipping and the machine doesn't need to be leveled. Gunk tends to accumulate on the rollers under the seat, which would probably go unnoticed if you don't pull the sled off and tip it up, but it's easy to clean.

I spent the first week focusing on correct technique and not killing myself. The machine comes with two booklets, a memory card, and a bottle of chain oil. The Indoor Rowing booklet has a lot of good information on proper form and suggested workouts starting from your very first day. There are also videos and active user forums on the Concept2 website. I've been following the suggestions, started slowly, set the damper at 3 and have left it there. Most nights I row from 25 to 40 minutes followed by stretching (recommended: AM/PM Stretch with Madeleine Lewis or AM Yoga for Your Week with Rodney Yee). I spent a lot of time on form and kept my stroke rate at about 18-19 spm. Slow, right? But I don't get sloppy and as I get stronger it seems that upping the stroke rate doesn't really improve my performance all that much. Before I started rowing, the morning routine was to get out of bed with cramping in my thigh and buttocks that nearly put me in tears. No joke: this disappeared overnight as soon as I started rowing. I felt a little soreness, mostly in my upper back, but zero lower back pain and no cramping AT ALL. One week of this was worth the $900.

The rowing machine puts you in total control of your workout in terms of how hard and how fast you want to work, and doesn't require you to do anything other than row harder or faster - there's no incline or speed buttons to push like with a treadmill. The rowing motion feels quite natural to me and time slides by. I actually look forward to my rowing time, and even though I'm still just getting started there is nothing about this that makes me feel like I won't be looking forward to my rowing time any less by next year. Plus, I expect by then I will be getting a lot more competitive about upping my pace. Update: Concept2 has a 100,000m between Thanksgiving and Christmas challenge. UPS delivered the Monday after Thanksgiving and without even trying I'm within 15K with 4 days to go. That's how cool rowing is.

If you're on the fence about which home exercise machine to buy, do yourself a favor and buy a rowing machine. Do yourself an additional favor and buy a Concept2.
text_fidelity_b: Concept2 Model D Indoor Rowing Machine (Gray)

text_fidelity_a:
XPRIT Electric Scooter, Up to 15 Miles Range, 3 Gear Speed Mode Alright, this is going to start off sounding rather negative, but I’d like to point you in the direction of the 4 stars above. If you stay with me throughout you’ll understand.

I’ve been through 3 of these now. The first one I purchased directly from the company, and it was black with softer tires (which felt great going over bumps, but not as great when riding and trying to keep up with friends using the same scooter but with the hard plastic tires found on this gray model.) I won’t review the black model here, just know that unless you’re around 150lbs or lessthe black model is slow af.

This model however, with the hard plastic tires is great. Quality control on the other hand is not as great. The first of the gray model that I got here through Amazon came in with an already cracked front fender. I figured no big deal, since it’s bound to eventually break off anyway (it cracked off of the black model on my second ride, and I wasn’t riding it on rough roads. They just crack and fall off sometimes. Or the screw loosens and it falls off. It’s a minor issue really, so long as it doesn’t get caught between the wheel and the fork and launch you...)

Next issue worthy of note... the screws provided want to loosen up and fall out after every other ride. The fix for this is locktite. It will save your life... perhaps literally. The last thing you want is to have your handlebars give out because all the screws fell out going down the road. It’s an extreme scenario, but a possible (and preventable) one.

My throttle got stuck in the “go” position, and I had to initiate an exchange because of it. It’s possible that the spring inside let go, or something when I went over a bump, but it really shouldn’t have. This issue needs to be addressed and updated for the next model.

Finally the brakes. Ah, what to say about the brakes? They’re good, for a couple of weeks if you live in a hilly area. But when they start to go, you’ll find yourself adjusting the brake cable almost daily. I’d like if XPRIT would release a disc and pad replacement that we could purchase, though I strongly suspect the xiaomi scooter’s brakes (m365 I think the scooter is called?) would probably be compatible. I’ll have to look into that eventually.

Now that we’ve gotten that unpleasantness out of the way... these are a blast to zip around on. My roommates and I all got them, and use them often to travel downtown to our favorite coffee shop, or for a late night snack a couple of miles away at the local gas station. They’re fun to ride, and when they’re well maintained they’re completely safe. You just have to be diligent, check your screws from time to time (daily) or use locktite around the thread, liberally applied, and just finger check the screws once a week or so to make sure they don’t feel like they’re loosening up. These things really do go pretty quick. Even in eco mode I thought it felt fast at first, then I discovered the red mode and realized they go even faster. Display reads out in KPH, not MPH, keep that in mind when riding.

This scooter is definitely worth the buy if you’re willing to risk having to send a couple of lemons back in order to find a good one. You might luck out on the first shot. Three of my roommates did. I have really bad luck sometimes haha.

Last but not least, any comments that mention seeing an E1 code, or similar, that happened to me on my first scooter too, it only happened for me when the battery ran out though, so it’s possible that’s what’s making it happen for others. Always fully charge before first use... or any use really.
text_fidelity_b: XPRIT Electric Scooter, Up to 15 Miles Range, 3 Gear Speed Mode

Zippo hand warmer is made in Taiwan, where as Hakukin(Peacock) is made in Japan by Hakukin for 80 years.
First imperssion of Zippo, looks just as cheap as Penguin(I think it was labeled as made in China). The burner looks different from Penguin or Hakukin.

I have to wonder why Hakukin is not sold in US? It seems to be available in England, why not in US? I would pay twice the price I paid for Zippo and still be happy with Hakukin.

There seems to be some organized effort by either the maker or the stores that sell them to rate down the negative reviews. Just look at the number of "Helpful".
Shameless.

Hakkin (Peacock) works!!!

The metal for the screws is so soft that when I attempted to do so (by hand) the screw head got stripped after a few turns. text_fidelity_a: Columbia Women's Boundary Bay Jacket First of all I have had a hard time with Columbia jackets. I have a long rain resistant jacket from them in XL and I have a hard time zipping it up over my chest area. I purchased this in an XL thinking it might fit like the other but I was wrong, its so soft and fluffy. I could probably go down to a size L and I might order it just to see what it would fit like. I am 5'3 and in-between a chubby/athletic build with 36DDD. Initially the jacket was puffier and fuller than I thought. There is lots of room in the arms, the arms are a tad longer for me but thats okay.  I purchased the black and I can say that the Grey color photo is probably the best representation of this fluffy full look. I have lots of room in the chest, back and armpit area. I could definitely wear a heavy carhartt style hoodie underneath and feel comfortable.  I am short so this does make me look boxier and shorter but I need something long and warm for those cold and wet high school football game nights in the Pacific Northwest. It frequently rains here and can get really cold and drop to the teens so I needed something warm and water resistant but did not want to wear a ski jacket. This jacket is definitely warm and I have not stood out in the pouring rain in this but it does repel water. I can not describe the cuffs, it is like a soft waterproof material and will be perfect if your sleeves get wet from the rain and the rain will just roll off. I initially wanted an omni heat silver lined jacket but this seems like it would keep me just as warm. The tail detail is a tad weird and I don't think it adds much style value but its a nice touch. The zipper is a double zipper so you can unzip it when sitting but honestly this would defeat the purpose for me because if I am sitting on the bleachers I want my thighs to be covered and warm. I found that even if I sat down I did not need to unzip the bottom half, probably because I purchased the XL, might not be the same if I picked the L. I wear a size 12 in jeans for size comparison. If you were to travel with this jacket it would be on the bulky side, must larger than a down filled jacket. I would recommend using a travel vacuum bag if you want to shrink it down while traveling.
text_fidelity_b: Columbia Women's Boundary Bay Jacket

The bottom is large and sort of rectangular, though, so if you're looking for something that's quick and easy to grab, use, and stow away you'd better have a holder with a larger than average compartment for it.  It does stand up well on the counter or table and it isn't as prone to tipping as I worried it might be.  The opening size and the fact that it does have corners makes giving it a thorough cleaning quite difficult if you are the sort to mix anything into your water and aren't very good about immediately rinsing it out after use.  If you use it for only straight water and rinse it often it would probably be fine.  I think the bottom could stand to be rounded off a bit more to eliminate those corners and the opening could definitely stand to be a bit larger though.

Regardless of where you try it, foregrip or the stock, it cannot hold the sling in place. A heavy duty rubber band is more effective than this at holding large straps.

I also believe the company is using a common practice of identifying an American made product, while not outwardly saying Made in America. I understand that an American flag doesn’t always mean made here, but this style is commonly used for such purposes. Seeing as the company's profile is based out of China I would safely say this product is made there.

Overall, I wouldn’t recommend this product for most. If your strap is very narrow and you would have at most one fold over it might work but be aware that if it rubs against something the magnets will let go. I would like to see the company use stronger magnets or possibly a small strip of Velcro to assist the magnets. In the meantime I will sew some Velcro to my existing one.
text_fidelity_b: Bugleman Rifle Sling Staging Strap Magnetic Sling Staging Solution

Right now I'm on a bit of a budget, so decided to go with the lower-featured FT1. I have to say I have been pleasantly surprised. After a little learning curve with the 1-button controls, I've found it easy to use, informative and the audible alarm is helpful.

The only thing I didn't love about my Polar FT1 was the chest strap it comes with. The higher end Polars come with a softer fabric strap, but the FT1 comes with a strap with a sort of flexible plastic piece on the front that isn't as form-fitting. It's not terrible - honest! - but it's not great, either. I ended up getting a Polar H7, and it works great with my FT1 plus I can simultaneously use it with various fitness apps on my phone; I like it best with Endomondo, which also sends your workout to My Fitness Pal.

The features I was looking for that the FT1 has:
A large-ish, easy to read display
An alarm you can set so you're alerted when your heart rate gets too high or too low during workouts
The ability to change your max heart rate
Comfortable wrist band

Overall I'm happy with my FT1, and even happier when I paired it with the Polar H7, but honestly it works fine with the strap it came with. I may upgrade someday, but for now my FT1 has/does everything I need and works great.

text_fidelity_a:
BalanceFrom High Density Premium Muscle Relaxation and Fitness Foam Roller I’m a big fan of SMR (self myofacial release) exercises and stretching. They are easy to do and only require a roller, such as this. I can’t address the specific about the exercises in this review (do a search for myofascial release to learn more about the techniques and how they accomplish trigger point release) but rather will address only the roller itself.

This is a good quality roller. It’s the standard 6 inch diameter and is basically (like most other rollers) indestructible. It is a little less dense than other high-density rollers I've used, which is not a bag thing. I prefer that the roller has a little bit of give to it, since the ones that are rock-hard can be uncomfortable. On the other hand, I know people who prefer the rock-hard ones, so it’s more of a personal preference than a “good” or “bad” feature.

The surface is has a slight texture to it, but feels good against the skin. I didn't encounter any rough spots in the foam.

Some rollers have nubs on them to help stimulate trigger release points. If you are new to rollers, I’d suggest getting a smooth one such as this to start. Nubs take a while to get used to, and some people (myself included) can never get used to them.

I have the full-size version and find that best for back and full-body exercises. The smaller version (which I did not use) is better for targeted routines for specific upper or lower body areas.

Unlike other foam rollers this had only a slight “chemical” smell to it when I removed it from the wrapper, and the smell dissipated quickly.

My only quibble is that the ends are not perfectly flat – there’s a small elevated area at each end (you can see that in the product photo) which is most likely an artifact of how these are manufactured. It has zero impact in how the product is used, but does make it a just a little bit tippy when you store it on-end. Again, minor point, and it does stand up on end without toppling over.

This is a good choice if you’re looking for a roller. (And, if you’re not familiar with SMR, do take a few minutes to run a search and read about it – it can really make a difference!).
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: BalanceFrom High Density Premium Muscle Relaxation and Fitness Foam Roller

text_fidelity_a:
RockTape RockBand Flex Ultra-durable Resistance Bands with Handles and Loops I had some of the latex bands previously. It was very frustrating when they snapped in the middle of my exercising. This does not seem to have the same problem. Let's take a look at how they worked out for me..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This set is the light gray padded elastic set. That means that there is a light resistance. This is what I needed to help my body ease back into flexibility after having some physical problems to overcome. There is a book that has photos which show how to use the bands in a variety of different ways.

WHAT IS THE MANUAL LIKE?
First of all the manual has photos of each exercise with an explanation. It also has explanations of each set of exercises, what it does for the body and what the basics of these systems in the body are like and how they work. The manual is easy to understand and does outline all of the exercises well. I do appreciate the explanations. I also appreciate the rock tape on some of the models so that it shows how to use that as well.

HOW WAS THIS TO WORK WITH?
Some of the exercises in this manual require that you have a place to attach the band securely to do them. That means you have to have a loop, hook, or other place to anchor the band to do some of the exercises. If you don't that eliminates a lot of the exercises. I found that this did help me to rehabilitate my body slowly and gradually without the fear of the bands snapping.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice non-breaking way of using bands for rehabilitation or gradual strength building. The manual helps to outline how to use the bands and give ideas how the body works and how the bands help.

MY RATING
Four stars for this. I would like the bands to be a little wider and more substantial than they are- they are a bit narrow. However, it does work well and I am glad to have used this set.
text_fidelity_b: RockTape RockBand Flex Ultra-durable Resistance Bands with Handles and Loops

Bowflex SelectTech 552 / 1090 Dumbbell Stand (Discontinued) The stand arrived very quickly and this is the only good thing I have to say about this product. At first I thought that I received a cheap knock-off because none of the parts looked like something BowFlex would put their name on to. The Instructions are a joke, they are fairly simple to follow, but, it is a photocopy of the original and because of that there are very little details in the pictures. None of the parts were labeled left or right (it doesn't really matter except for the dumbbell platforms). The manual said there were supposed to be 4 different sizes of screws, I only had 3 sizes. The right and left sides supposed to be symmetrical; mine were way off, resulting in the stand leaning to one side even with the adjustment screw on one of the feet unscrewed as far as possible. All the feet were welded crookedly. I did not tighten any of the screw all the way until the end in order for everything to come together correctly and even then I had to bend the back plate in order to attach it. Technically the stand is very easy to assemble, but since nothing aligns correctly it takes way logger to put together than it should and is more difficult. At the end it does what it supposed to if you don't count the fact that it is leaning to one side. Not what I expected from BowFlex.

Update: Today I saw a real stand in a local store and I can say with total certainty that these are fakes. They do not look anything like the original, the metal is a lot thinner and the quality is nowhere near as good as the original. Shame on you Amazon for selling knock-off's...

Camping Tent 2-4 People, Waterproof and Windproof Family Tents, Outdoor & Travel, Easy Setup Removable Rainfly, Ventilated Windows for Camping, Portable with Carry Bag I have the "3-4" person option. I chose this after carefully considering the dimensions. In my experience, I get 3 person tents for just myself. I am tall and wide, and want room to move, and have space for gear. The difference between their 2 person tent and "3-4" person tent is not much in one direction, but it adds quite a bit of space in another. So no matter what, if you have 2 people and get the two people tent you will be shoulder to shoulder, and if you 3 people for a 3 person tent, you will be shoulder to shoulder. So where does a 4th person go? Along the 3 peoples feet (or head). I wont be person #4. haha
SIZE :
2 people (82.67" X 59.05" X 47.24")
4 people (86.67" X 82.67" X 59.05" )

That being said, I got the 3-4 person tent for use for myself and my 2 large labs. Not necessarily for camping (though will do for that), but as a prep item in case the electric goes out or heat goes out. Sleeping can be much more comfortable (and survivable) if the space around you is reduced. So furnace out in a blizzard? House getting real cold? Get layered up, set up a tent INSIDE the house (or even on the bed, or make a layered bed roll), and your body heat will be contained. Add a handful of cats and a couple of big labs, and we have a toasty sweat lodge, haha. Not sure where my husband will sleep. He can have a bivvy on other side of room, haha.

Internal hook for hanging a light. Bag is big enough to be able to get the tent back inside.

I happen to already have a couple of tents of this size, but I have had them for like 20 years and I havent used them in about 10 years.. so I wanted to "freshen up" my preps. Had a little sticker shock, but this seamed to be reasonable price for the size I chose. The two person appears doable if for 1 person and some gear, or a couple of slim people who like each other a lot. The 3/4 person is more for me and my preferences. I keep a tent in my car. I have kept one as an emergency item since I first began driving as a teen. Now in my 40s, it is just a habit. I can sleep in my car, but I am a big fan of options. Many times I went camping on the fly because I had everything I needed in my trunk. Still do. Why not?

4 stars because everything looks good. I havent truly put it through its paces yet. I dont expect it to fall apart. I have had dirt cheap tents last forever, so I just expect this to hold up. I'll update if I learn anything else.

Caboodles Tote I selected this bag to replace my laptop bag, which was taken by my college-age son when his previous bag failed him. My personal preference in bags is actually a messenger style bag, not a tote, so I wasn’t sure if this would be my new go-to bag or if I needed to keep shopping. It has proven to be a good bag and I am mostly happy with it.

This bag is large enough to handle a 15” laptop, but it is better suited for a smaller-sized laptop or tablet. It isn’t going to handle anything bigger, the limiting dimension being the height, unless you’re content with not zipping the bag or having the contents obstruct the handles. Of course there is room to put others things in the bag with said laptop too, so it’s not just a laptop sleeve.

The bag itself is made of a tight nylon weave with vinyl handles, a vinyl divider and an outside vinyl pocket. It is not impervious to cuts and nicks but the nylon is fine enough that it should resist most hazards such as desk corners. I looked this bag over very carefully and found no cuts, nicks or blemishes in the materials, the stitching is straight and there are no loose threads. Overall, it is made well.

If I could change two things...I would have used canvas instead of nylon which holds up better to frequent use and tends to be stronger. Time will tell if this bag will withstand steady use, but so far it’s faring well enough and showing no signs of fatigue. Also, I would have reinforced the bottom with a heavier material which is the one place where this bag seems most likely to eventually fail.

My preference in bags is still a messenger bag; that said, this is a decent bag that seems to be made well and is large enough to handle my laptop. If you prefer a tote bag to either a messenger or backpack, this one is worth consideration.
text_fidelity_b: Caboodles Tote
